newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine said scrapping sugar beet reform plan.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine said scrapping sugar beet reform plan.

text.p: Ukraine has scrapped a plan to save its troubled sugar sector by doubling domestic prices and guaranteeing minimum prices to sugar beet producers, a Western analyst said on Tuesday.
"That whole plan has fallen apart," said Bohdan Chomiak of Chemonics International, a U.S.-funded group working to promote reform in Ukraine's agricultural sector. "They issued a formal resolution."

The plan, announced earlier this year, would have limited domestic sugar sales to 1.5 million tonnes and charged a government-set minimum price of 1.19 hryvnias per kilo, as well as paying producers 70 hryvnias per tonne of sugar beet.

But Agriculture Minister Yuri Karasyk said earlier this month the cash-strapped government was still seeking ways to finance the plan, which baffled traders and earned criticism from producers, who called it an attempt by the government to grab more control of the market.
Local media reported that Ukraine also faced pressure to scrap the plan from the World Bank, currently financing agricultural reform programmes in the former Soviet republic.
Ukraine is overrun with domestic sugar that is expensive to produce in its ageing refineries.

The former Soviet republic has lost most of its market since Russia, traditionally the largest buyer of Ukrainian sugar, slapped large tariffs on it after accusing its neighbour of dumping on its market.
Ukraine is forecast to produce 3.26 million tonnes of refined sugar this year, flat on 1996 levels, from a sugar beet crop of 27 million tonnes after it produced 24 million tonnes of beets last year.
The plan also called for reduced sowing of sugar beets in the future to reduce oversupply, and said sugar not sold on the domestic market would be sold abroad at world prices.
